title: Leviticus
summary: Leviticus is a biblical book focused on holiness, sacrifice, priesthood, purity, atonement, and life with God.
historical_context: Leviticus forms Israel for holy worship and covenant life in the Lord's presence.
ancient_near_east_context: Leviticus belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Leviticus should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Leviticus as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Torah, book 3 of 5, Leviticus contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting holiness, sacrifice, priesthood, purity, atonement, and life with God to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Leviticus as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Leviticus uses law within Torah, book 3 of 5 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Leviticus helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Many scholars see a composite work shaped over time
date_ranges: Critical: final shaping often placed in the exilic or post-exilic period
original_audience: Israel formed by covenant and delivered into the land promise
historical_setting: The Exodus, wilderness, and land-promise setting of the Torah
canonical_role: Leviticus anchors holiness, sacrifice, priesthood, purity, atonement, and life with God within Torah, book 3 of 5 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How to read narrative and law together

related_objects.notes: Priestly ministry organizes much of the book.
Holiness is the book's defining theme.
Levitical service belongs to the book's cultic setting.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Leviticus first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
The relationship links on Leviticus are orientation anchors, not a full interpretive outline of the book.
